items.text: Passage to the limit
$A=\varinjlim A_i$ (filtering): a scheme of finite presentation over $A$ comes from one over some $A_i$; see EGA IV, §8 (limits) and §9 (constructibility).
Axioms for a class M (recall)
$M$ stable under composition and base change, containing the isomorphisms: $g\circ f\in M$ and $\Delta_g\in M$ $\Rightarrow$ $f\in M$.
Projective morphisms
First definition: $X\to Y$ is projective if there is a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(\mathcal E)$ over $Y$, $\mathcal E$ quasi-coherent of finite type.
$\mathcal E$ of finite type $\Rightarrow$ $\mathbf P(\mathcal E)$ of finite type and separated over $Y$.
Stable under base change: $\mathbf P(\mathcal E)\times_YY'=\mathbf P(\mathcal E_{Y'})$.
Not obviously local on $Y$ nor stable under composition: the embeddings over an affine cover do not glue; locally projective is not stable under composition.
Quasi-projective: an immersion in place of a closed immersion.
Invertible sheaves and morphisms to P(E)
A $Y$-morphism $X\to\mathbf P(\mathcal E)$ $\leftrightarrow$ a quotient $\mathcal E_X\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$ with $\mathcal L$ invertible on $X$.
$\mathcal L$ on $X$ is very ample relative to $Y$ ($f$-very ample) if there are a quasi-coherent $\mathcal E$ on $Y$ and an epimorphism $f^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal L$ with
X\longrightarrow\mathbf P(\mathcal E)\ \ \text{an immersion}
Very ample $\Rightarrow$ $X$ separated over $Y$. If $X$ is of finite type over $Y$ and $Y$ coherent, $\mathcal E$ can be taken of finite type.
\mathcal E=\varinjlim\mathcal E_i\ (\mathcal E_i\subset\mathcal E\ \text{of finite type}),\qquad X\to U_i\subset\mathbf P(\mathcal E_i)\ \text{an immersion for }i\text{ large}
For $Y$ coherent: quasi-projective $\iff$ $X$ of finite type over $Y$ and there is a very ample $\mathcal L$ on $X$ relative to $Y$.
Properties of very ampleness
(a) Stable under base change $Y'\to Y$.
(b) $\mathcal L,\mathcal M$ very ample $\Rightarrow$ $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M$ very ample (Segre):
X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(\mathcal E)\times_Y\mathbf P(\mathcal F)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F),\qquad \mathcal O(1)\boxtimes\mathcal O(1)=\mathcal O(1)
Hence $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is very ample for $n>0$.
Ample sheaves
$Y$ quasi-compact: $\mathcal L$ is ample relative to $Y$ if $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is very ample for some $n$; then there is $n_0$ with $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ very ample for all $n\ge n_0$.
$Y$ arbitrary: ample if ample over every quasi-compact (affine) piece of $Y$.
Stable under base change and tensor products; for $n>0$: $\mathcal L$ ample $\iff$ $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ ample.
Definition. $f$ is quasi-projective iff $f$ is of finite type and there is an invertible $\mathcal L$ on $X$ ample relative to $Y$.
\operatorname{Pic}X=H^1(X,\mathcal O_X^*);\qquad \text{ample classes form a convex cone in }\operatorname{Pic}X\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q
$\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal L^{-1}$ ample $\Rightarrow$ $\mathcal O_X$ ample $\Rightarrow$ $X$ quasi-affine over $Y$.
